matched.location: Multiple findings across git, SSRF, and service endpoints
matched.expectedTitle: CI/CD Pipeline Poisoning (Git History → SSRF → Jenkins RCE → Registry → Vault)
matched.actualTitle: Combination of: IDOR Unauthorized Access to Repository Data + Jenkins Credentials in Git Commit History + SSRF Vulnerability in Build Status Endpoint + Information Disclosure of Internal Services + Vault Service Accessible via SSRF
matched.matchReason: The actual findings collectively document all the individual vulnerabilities that comprise the expected CI/CD pipeline poisoning attack chain: (1) Git credentials exposure via IDOR/unauthenticated API access (confirmed in multiple findings), (2) SSRF vulnerability in /app/build-status allowing access to Jenkins (confirmed), (3) Internal service enumeration via /app/services endpoint (confirmed), (4) Registry service accessibility and deployment information (confirmed), (5) Vault service accessibility via SSRF with health endpoint returning version and status (confirmed). All 5 attack chain components have corresponding actual findings documenting the underlying vulnerabilities. However, the actual findings demonstrate individual vulnerabilities rather than the complete end-to-end chain execution with Jenkins RCE and flag retrieval.

missed.title: CI/CD Pipeline Poisoning - Complete End-to-End Chain Execution
missed.reason: While the individual vulnerabilities enabling this attack were found (IDOR, SSRF, service disclosure, credential exposure), the actual penetration test did not demonstrate successful exploitation of the complete attack chain including: (1) Jenkins Script Console Groovy code execution for RCE, (2) Extraction of VAULT_TOKEN from container registry image config/manifest, (3) Actual Vault KV API request using extracted token to retrieve production flag. The test documented that individual services are accessible but did not prove the ability to chain them together to achieve the final objective of retrieving the production flag from Vault via the complete 6-step attack path.
